name: Donald J. Trump for President

summary.text: Donald J. Trump for President was Donald Trump's principal campaign committee for the 2016 election (and later his 2020 committee). FEC data as reported by NPR show it paid Cambridge Analytica $5.9 million for data management and survey research; its largest 2016 vendor was Brad Parscale's firm Giles-Parscale, paid nearly $88 million. The committee has said it used RNC voter data rather than Cambridge Analytica's, and it has been the subject of Campaign Legal Center complaints to the FEC that remain allegations.

facts.claim: NPR reported that the Trump campaign paid Cambridge Analytica a total of $5.9 million, according to FEC data processed by the Center for Responsive Politics, and that the campaign's filings say the firm provided data management and survey research.
facts.quote: the Trump campaign paid the firm a total of $5.9 million, according to Federal Election Commission data processed by the nonprofit Center for Responsive Politics

facts.claim: Giles-Parscale was the campaign committee's top vendor in the 2016 cycle, paid nearly $88 million by the committee according to FEC filings reported by CNBC; Brad Parscale was named digital media director in June 2016.
facts.quote: the campaign shelled out the majority of the money, nearly $88 million

facts.claim: Jared Kushner told Forbes in May 2017 that in formalizing the digital operation after the primary, 'We brought in Cambridge Analytica.' In March 2018 a campaign spokesperson told ABC News that the campaign used the RNC for its voter data and not Cambridge Analytica; CNN reported Cambridge Analytica data was used for some targeted digital advertising and a large TV buy before the campaign switched to RNC data in autumn 2016.
facts.quote: used the RNC for its voter data and not Cambridge Analytica

facts.claim: The Campaign Legal Center's FEC complaints (MUR 7147) allege that the super PAC Make America Number 1 coordinated unlawfully with the Trump campaign through their shared vendor Cambridge Analytica and through payments linked to Steve Bannon and Kellyanne Conway; NPR noted that a campaign and a super PAC may lawfully hire the same vendor. No FEC finding was located.
facts.quote: made unlawful and unreported expenditures in coordination with the campaign

facts.claim: In July 2020 the Campaign Legal Center filed a complaint alleging the campaign hid nearly $170 million of spending by routing it through American Made Media Consultants and other firms linked to Brad Parscale; the campaign said it reports all payments to AMMC as required by the FEC.
